Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 36, verses 1–2:

Lesson No. 205: Explanation of the Verses

1 to 29

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

"Ya-Sin. By the Wise Quran..." to "...and We have enumerated everything in a clear register" (1–12)

Allah swears by two letters, "Ya" and "Sin", and likewise swears by the Quran. Here Allah has joined these letters and the Quran together in the oath. This gives preference to the interpretation of the muqatta'at (the disjointed letters at the beginning of certain surahs) that we have adopted with reference to these letters. The connection between the mention of these letters and the mention of the Quran is that this Quran is composed of these very letters. This is also proof that the Quran is from Allah. Through this, the Quran draws the attention of those who do not reflect upon it, so that they may consider this point: that the Quran has been made from these very letters that are within your reach. Yet the Quran's manner of expression, its style of discourse and its logical reasoning are such that you have been left unable to produce a speech like it.

The attribute of the Quran mentioned here, after the oath, is wisdom (hikmah). Wisdom is the attribute of a being who possesses intellect, who is living and wise. By stating this attribute of the Quran, the intended impression is that this is a book that is living and possesses purpose and will. For this reason it is wise. Although this attribute is used for the Quran in a metaphorical sense (majaz), it manifests a great reality. An important truth is being brought close to the minds: that this book has a soul and a life. When the heart of the reader becomes pure and he converses with it in love, this book speaks with the person with great affection and love, and then it unfolds its secrets to such a person, provided the reader himself opens his heart for it and becomes its own with his whole heart and soul. Then the reader will see in it those features that a person sees in the face of a friend. He will be drawn to this book with the same longing with which one is drawn to a friend, and then he finds in the Quran the same tranquillity that he finds in the gathering of a friend. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) liked to hear the Quran recited by others. He would stand at the doors from which the recitation of the wise Quran could be heard, and would listen, just as a lover listens closely to the words of his beloved.

The Quran is indeed wise. It speaks to every person who becomes its devotee. It plucks the sensitive strings of a believer's heart. It converses with him to the extent that he needs. And this conversation is conducted with great wisdom, in such a manner that the one addressed is reformed and is given a direction.

The Quran, being wise, trains with great wisdom: in a most reasonable manner, in the correct psychological direction, in a manner in which all human capacities are left open in a constructive way, and human capacities are given a direction for healthy growth. It gives mankind a most wise system for living, within whose open and wide boundaries a person carries on the activities of life. Allah, by swearing by "Ya" and "Sin" and then by the Quran, gives assurance that, O Messenger, you are among the messengers, and revelation is being sent down upon you. You are the noble Messenger, and this is the Wise Quran.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah Ya-Sin, verses 3–4:

﴿Innaka laman al-mursalin﴾ ... ﴿ala siratin mustaqim﴾ (36:3–4) "Indeed, you are among the messengers, upon a straight path."

What need does Allah have to swear an oath? Yet this oath, sworn by the Qur'an and by its letters, confers dignity upon the things about which the oath is sworn. For it is the way of Allah that He swears by something great and important, until the importance of that thing becomes a witness and a confirmation.

﴿Innaka laman al-mursalin﴾ (36:3) "Indeed, you are among the messengers." From the manner in which this verse comes, it becomes clear that with Allah the sending of messengers and their selection has already been determined. Here the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is addressed in the form of a declaration of his being, informing that his name is in the list of the messengers, and rather than addressing the deniers and rejecters, the Messenger of Allah is addressed directly. This conveys the impression that the messengership and the office of prophethood are so exalted that no debate, discussion or contention can be raised concerning them. Simply the Messenger being informed by Allah is itself complete proof.

﴿Innaka laman al-mursalin ... ala siratin mustaqim﴾ (36:3–4) "Indeed, you are among the messengers, upon a straight path." After the appointment and designation of the messengers, it is stated what the nature of messengership is: that it is a straight path. This messengership is straight like the edge of a sword. There is in it no crookedness and no deviation. It has neither complexity nor flexibility. It consists of a truth that is entirely clear, and there is in it no ambiguity. It does not follow base desires, nor does it change its direction according to expediency. Whoever seeks this truth sincerely will find it.

Since this messengership shows a straight path, there is in it no confusion, no complexity and no winding. It does not make matters difficult, nor does it place people in hardships. Within it there is no dialectical debate on contested issues, and it does not entangle one in philosophical notions. It presents the truth in an extremely simple form, and in such a simple form that contains no doubt and no false argument, so simple that it needs no further explanation. Manipulation of words and drawing one thing out of another have no place in it, nor are intricate and tangled ideas brought under discussion. By this messengership, life can be lived by acting upon the present guidance and apparent commandments. It is guidance for both the unlettered and the learned; it is guidance for both the villager and the city dweller. Every person and every class finds in it the guidance of their need, and with it their life is set right. Their system of life is put in order, their ways of living are corrected, and human relations are conducted with great ease.

Furthermore, this messengership is also in harmony with the nature of this universe and with the divine law flowing through it. It is also in harmony with human beings and with the things found in the human environment. It neither conflicts with the things of the world, nor does it command man to conflict with nature. It is rightly established upon its own method, and it runs parallel to this universe. It is supportive; it gives a system which is a complete universe.

This messengership shows the correct path to Allah, and it leads to Allah. Those who follow this messengership never face the danger of forgetting the way. No crookedness comes in their path, for whoever enters this valley, passing through its ups and downs, reaches straight to the pleasure of Allah and to his Great Creator. This messengership has given this Qur'an, which draws the complete map of this straight path and is a guide. When a person walks under the guidance of this Book, he attains a straight understanding of truth. He turns toward Allah, and then this Book gives decisive guidance concerning its values and places every thing in its right place.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 36, verses 5–6:

تنزیل العزیز الرحیم (36: 5) "It is a revelation from the Mighty, the Merciful" ("This is sent down by the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful"). In such passages Allah introduces Himself to His servants so that they may understand the reality of the Word of Allah: that Allah is Mighty and that He is Merciful. He is Mighty, so He can do whatever He wills. And He is Merciful, so He deals with His servants with mercy. Therefore there is always an aspect of mercy in the commands of Allah. As for the purposes of the revelation of this Qur'an and its wisdom, they are simply these: to warn people of an evil end and to convey the message of truth to them. Especially

لتنذر قوما۔۔۔۔ فھم غفلون (36: 6) "So that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, and therefore they are heedless" ("That you may warn a people whose fathers were never warned, so they remain heedless"). Heedlessness (ghaflah) is that great disease which causes corruption in hearts. A heedless heart, in reality, abandons its duty of office, and so it becomes an idle organ, because taking guidance and accepting it is the work of the heart. When the proofs of guidance are presented before people, the human heart either passes over them heedlessly or it takes them in. Therefore, warning these heedless people was beneficial, because generations had passed and no warner had come to this people. No one had come who would admonish them. These people were among the ummah and offspring of Hazrat Ibrahim (peace be upon him). And centuries had passed after them, and no prophet or warner had come to them. Therefore a warner of this kind was a necessity for them, one who would thoroughly awaken them from heedlessness, since from the time of their forefathers these people had been lying in the sleep of heedlessness.

After this it is told what the end of these heedless people is to be: what decision the system of qadar (divine decree) has made concerning them, because Allah had full knowledge of their hearts. He knew in advance the matters that would proceed from them. What they did was also within Allah's knowledge, and what was going to happen was also within His knowledge.

The Quranic verse (36:7) is quoted as: "Indeed, the word has come into effect upon most of them, so they do not believe."

Surely the sentence has been passed against most of them, and so they do not believe. Allah has issued His decree concerning them, and Allah's decree regarding them is just. This judgment was based on truth; it is in accordance with the truth. For Allah knew their reality well. Allah was also aware of their awareness and their inclinations. These people were never going to believe. This is the fate of the majority. Veils have come to stand between their souls and guidance. They can neither see the proofs of the truth, nor do they possess the awareness of them.

The picture of the psychological state of those upon whom Allah's decree has become binding is this: there are yokes around their necks, and within those yokes they are bound up to their chins. They cannot even see. Barriers and veils between them and guidance have come to stand over them. Veils have fallen over their eyes, so they are no longer capable of learning.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 36, verses 8–9:

"We have put yokes around their necks, reaching up to their chins, so they are held with their heads raised. We have set a barrier before them and a barrier behind them, and We have covered them, so they cannot see." (36:8–9)

Their hands are bound to the yokes. Then these are fastened to their necks and clamped beneath their chins. In this way their heads are forced upward. Therefore they are unable to look down at the path in front of them. Since they are in this wretched state, they can neither see nor do anything. Then there is a wall before them and a wall behind them. In this way they are no longer able to reach the truth in any way. They are shackled, so they cannot see. There are walls in front and behind, through which their gaze cannot pass. Through their own incapacity and wrongdoing they have arrived at this psychological state.

This scene is sensory and a very intense one, but in everyday life we meet countless people about whom one reaches the conclusion that they are unable to see the clear truth. Therefore, veils and walls such as these stand between them and the truth, so that they cannot see through them. Even if their hands and feet are not bound in this way, and their heads are not fixed so that they can only look upward, but they appear outwardly sound, whole and free, their psychological state is still of this kind: they cannot see guidance through their insight, and between the proofs of guidance and their thinking there appear to be invisible walls. This was the very condition of those people of Makkah who received the Qur'an with this same psychological state. The Qur'an set before them clear proofs and signs, and they remained obstinate in denial. Apart from the proofs presented, the Qur'an itself was a miraculous proof and sign, before which no person of insight could stand, yet these people persisted in denial.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 36, verse 10:

"It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe" (36:10). This is because Allah had already decided their case, since Allah knew that there was no way for guidance to reach their hearts to faith. Warning has no effect upon hearts that are not prepared to accept faith: hearts that are bound, with walls standing between them and the truth. The dead hearts cannot be brought to life through warning and preaching; rather, the heedless and the sleeping can be awakened, especially those sleeping hearts that wish to receive guidance and are ready for it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 36, verse 11:

"You can only warn the one who follows the Reminder and fears the Most Merciful unseen. So give him the good news of forgiveness and a generous reward" (36:11). Here "the Reminder" (al-Dhikr) refers to the Noble Qur'an. This is the preferred opinion. The one who follows the Qur'an and fears the Most Merciful without having seen Him is the one who can benefit from warning. It is as if he is the very person for whom the warning has come, and it is for such a person that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent. Although the message is general, barriers have come to stand between other people and guidance. Therefore guidance has become confined to the one who accepts the Qur'an and fears the Most Merciful unseen. When such people benefit from the warning, they become worthy of good news.

"So give him the good news of forgiveness and a generous reward" (36:11). Forgiveness is for the mistakes that have occurred, provided they were not persisted in. A generous reward is because this person kept fearing Allah in private, and kept following the reminders that came from Allah. These two qualities are inseparable in the heart of the believer. Whenever the fear of God arises in a heart, a person begins to act upon God's guidance, and he attains steadfastness in the system of life that He has willed.

Accordingly, here a reminder is given that one day you will have to appear before God, and your reckoning will be prepared with utmost care, and nothing from it will be left out.

﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, and We record what they have sent forward and what they have left behind. And We have enumerated everything in a clear register﴾ (36:12). "Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life. We are recording the deeds they have done, and We are also recording the traces they have left behind. We have set down everything in a manifest book."

The revival of the dead is a matter that has always been the subject of debate. In this surah too, several examples will be given of its possibility. Here they are warned that whatever deeds they are performing, and whatever good or bad traces they are leaving behind, all of them are being recorded with God. Nothing from these deeds can be omitted, nor can it be forgotten. It is God who brings the dead to life. It is He who is recording their deeds and traces. It is He who is writing down everything. Therefore, all these matters will come to pass in exactly the way that God will manifest them with His own power, and in the way that God has taken upon Himself to manifest these matters.

By the "Clear Book" (Imam Mubin) is meant the Preserved Tablet (Lawh Mahfuz), or the register in which deeds are recorded according to God's system. By the Preserved Tablet is meant God's eternal and primordial knowledge, and God's knowledge encompasses everything.

Following the emphatic statement on the matter of revelation and prophethood, and the firm declaration of the question of accountability, the same theme is now presented in the form of a story. In this story, the two mutually opposed positions of faith and disbelief that emerge leave very deep impressions on the human soul, and the outcome of both positions can be seen as though etched before one's eyes.

﴿وَاضْرِبْ لَهُم مَّثَلًا أَصْحَابَ الْقَرْيَةِ إِذْ جَاءَهَا الْمُرْسَلُونَ ... بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌ مُّسْرِفُونَ﴾ (13–19)

The messengers said: "Our Lord knows that we have indeed been sent to you as messengers, and our only responsibility is to convey the message clearly." The people of the town said: "We regard you as a bad omen for us. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and you will suffer a painful punishment at our hands." The messengers replied: "Your bad omen is attached to yourselves. Do you say these things because you have been admonished? In truth, you are a people who have transgressed all bounds."

The Qur'an has not named the people of the town, nor the town itself. Regarding it, the exegetes have related many narrations. There is no need to pursue these narrations here, nor is there any need to discuss them. The fact that the Qur'an does not name this town is itself evidence that naming the village adds nothing to the purposes of the story. For this reason the Qur'an did not name the town or its location, and was content with the story and the lesson derived from it. In any case, it was a village to which two messengers were sent, just as Musa and his brother Harun (peace be upon them both) were both sent to Pharaoh and his chiefs. The people of the village denied these messengers. Allah sent a third messenger in support of the two messengers, and this third one informed the people that these two were truthful messengers. Thus the three of them began their call afresh.

﴿فَقَالُوا إِنَّا إِلَيْكُم مُّرْسَلُونَ﴾ (36:14) "They all said: We have been sent to you as messengers."

Now the people of the village raised against them the same worn-out objections that are always raised against messengers.

﴿قَالُوا مَا أَنتُمْ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُنَا وَمَا أَنزَلَ الرَّحْمَٰنُ مِن شَيْءٍ إِنْ أَنتُمْ إِلَّا تَكْذِبُونَ﴾ (36:15) "The people of the town said: You are nothing but human beings like us, and the Most Merciful has sent down nothing. You are merely lying."

On reflection upon these objections, which have been raised against all messengers, it becomes evident that these people were very simple-minded and their thinking immature. These people held strange notions about messengers and prophethood. In their view, the personality of a messenger should be a mysterious personality, and many illusions and stories should be attributed to his personality. Because a messenger comes from the heavens to the people of the earth, his personality must necessarily be associated with illusions and legends. How could it be that a messenger is an open and simple human being, with no secret in his life and no wonder in it, like us? How can a messenger be an ordinary and common human being like us, who walks in the markets and lives in houses like ours?

This was the simplicity of their thought and their reasoning. For prophethood does not necessarily entail mystery. Yet the station of messengership is not as simple as these people supposed. Within the office of messengership and the office of prophethood there is also a great and profound secret, and it is this: Allah Most High creates in an ordinary, simple human being such a capacity that, despite being an ordinary human, he becomes fit to receive revelation from the Creator. And this is more wondrous than that a messenger should be an angel, as these people proposed, that a messenger ought to be an angel.

The truth is that the purpose of messengership is to acquaint people with the Islamic system of life, and the life of the messenger is the practical model of this system, and the call of the messenger is that he invites people to follow this practical system. Since people are human, their leader too must be human, so that he may present a practical example for them and they may be able to emulate him.

This is why the life of every messenger is an open book for the people. The Qur'an, which is the firm Book of Allah, recorded a small and principled part of this detailed life; it wrote down principles rather than details. The rest of the detailed system of life the ummah derives from the practical life of the messenger of its time, and that practical life lies before the whole ummah as an open book and extends over many years. Within these details, the features of the messenger's family and domestic life and the patterns of his communal life are all present. At times the Qur'an has even recorded the psychological states of the messenger, so that coming generations may see what the inner state of the Trustworthy Prophet was.

Following the emphatic statement on the matter of revelation and prophethood, and the firm declaration of the question of accountability, the same theme is now presented in the form of a story. In this story, the two mutually opposed positions of faith and disbelief that emerge leave very deep impressions on the human soul, and the outcome of both positions can be seen as though etched before one's eyes.

﴿وَاضْرِبْ لَهُم مَّثَلًا أَصْحَابَ الْقَرْيَةِ إِذْ جَاءَهَا الْمُرْسَلُونَ ... بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌ مُّسْرِفُونَ﴾ (13–19)

The messengers said: "Our Lord knows that we have indeed been sent to you as messengers, and our only responsibility is to convey the message clearly." The people of the town said: "We regard you as a bad omen for us. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and you will suffer a painful punishment at our hands." The messengers replied: "Your bad omen is attached to yourselves. Do you say these things because you have been admonished? In truth, you are a people who have transgressed all bounds."

The Qur'an has not named the people of the town, nor the town itself. Regarding it, the exegetes have related many narrations. There is no need to pursue these narrations here, nor is there any need to discuss them. The fact that the Qur'an does not name this town is itself evidence that naming the village adds nothing to the purposes of the story. For this reason the Qur'an did not name the town or its location, and was content with the story and the lesson derived from it. In any case, it was a village to which two messengers were sent, just as Musa and his brother Harun (peace be upon them both) were both sent to Pharaoh and his chiefs. The people of the village denied these messengers. Allah sent a third messenger in support of the two messengers, and this third one informed the people that these two were truthful messengers. Thus the three of them began their call afresh.

﴿فَقَالُوا إِنَّا إِلَيْكُم مُّرْسَلُونَ﴾ (36:14) "They all said: We have been sent to you as messengers."

Now the people of the village raised against them the same worn-out objections that are always raised against messengers.

﴿قَالُوا مَا أَنتُمْ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُنَا وَمَا أَنزَلَ الرَّحْمَٰنُ مِن شَيْءٍ إِنْ أَنتُمْ إِلَّا تَكْذِبُونَ﴾ (36:15) "The people of the town said: You are nothing but human beings like us, and the Most Merciful has sent down nothing. You are merely lying."

On reflection upon these objections, which have been raised against all messengers, it becomes evident that these people were very simple-minded and their thinking immature. These people held strange notions about messengers and prophethood. In their view, the personality of a messenger should be a mysterious personality, and many illusions and stories should be attributed to his personality. Because a messenger comes from the heavens to the people of the earth, his personality must necessarily be associated with illusions and legends. How could it be that a messenger is an open and simple human being, with no secret in his life and no wonder in it, like us? How can a messenger be an ordinary and common human being like us, who walks in the markets and lives in houses like ours?

This was the simplicity of their thought and their reasoning. For prophethood does not necessarily entail mystery. Yet the station of messengership is not as simple as these people supposed. Within the office of messengership and the office of prophethood there is also a great and profound secret, and it is this: Allah Most High creates in an ordinary, simple human being such a capacity that, despite being an ordinary human, he becomes fit to receive revelation from the Creator. And this is more wondrous than that a messenger should be an angel, as these people proposed, that a messenger ought to be an angel.

The truth is that the purpose of messengership is to acquaint people with the Islamic system of life, and the life of the messenger is the practical model of this system, and the call of the messenger is that he invites people to follow this practical system. Since people are human, their leader too must be human, so that he may present a practical example for them and they may be able to emulate him.

This is why the life of every messenger is an open book for the people. The Qur'an, which is the firm Book of Allah, recorded a small and principled part of this detailed life; it wrote down principles rather than details. The rest of the detailed system of life the ummah derives from the practical life of the messenger of its time, and that practical life lies before the whole ummah as an open book and extends over many years. Within these details, the features of the messenger's family and domestic life and the patterns of his communal life are all present. At times the Qur'an has even recorded the psychological states of the messenger, so that coming generations may see what the inner state of the Trustworthy Prophet was.

This was the clear and easily understood truth against which people have always raised objections. Thus the inhabitants of that town said to the three messengers:

﴿You are nothing but human beings like us﴾ (36:15). "You are merely claiming that you are messengers. Now let us see the messengers' reply. They answer like men who know the reality of the situation, calm and confident."

This is the example of those rebellious people who always stand in the way of the Islamic call and resort to oppression. Whenever the Islamic call begins, people of this kind become active. This is the way of the work of calling to Allah. In contrast to them, there is another type among humans who accepts admonition, obeys it, and fears the Most Merciful without having seen Him. If he were not truthful, why would he unnecessarily bear these difficulties? This line of thought and these questions belong to a nature that has become conscious of the Creator of the universe, that has found the purpose of its existence and has become fully attached to it. Then its call is this:

Wa-ma li la a'budu alladhi fataranī (36:22): "Why should I not worship the One who created me?" Why should I turn away, in the end, from the natural path that has taken root in my heart? For there is a pull within the human being towards the One who created him. First of all, human nature turns towards God, the Creator. If nature deviates from this path, its causes are external, and these misleading causes and influences do not lie within human nature itself. Turning towards the Creator is nature's first and best impulse. It exists within nature, and it needs no external stimulus or influence. The human self naturally inclines towards Him. When faith enters someone's heart, he feels his Creator in the depths of his self. This statement of the believing man is the manifestation of that natural inclination. Without hesitation, he cries out: why should I not worship this Creator?

Sound human nature also perceives that in the end human beings must return to their Creator. Everything returns to its origin. That is why he says: wa-ilayhi turja'un (36:22): "And to Him you all will be returned." The natural reasoning is this: why should I not worship the One who created me? Since you all must return to Him, for your Creator is also He, and it is also your right to worship Him.

Now this man also comments on their hostile attitude: my attitude and my thinking are reasonable and natural, and if you adopt an attitude contrary to it, that would be against nature and misguided.

Lesson 206: An Overview

The previous lesson spoke of those who received the Islamic call with denial and rejection, and it described their fate by recounting the story of their town, and how those who denied were destroyed. Their end was that

﴿فَإِذَا هُمْ خَامِدُونَ﴾ (36:29) "suddenly they were extinguished, like dying embers."

But in this lesson the fate of the deniers of all communities and all heavenly scriptures is depicted. Here the features and marks of misguided people throughout the whole of human history are described, and here, in a most heart-rending voice and manner, a call is made: how strange it is that people do not learn lessons from the history of those nations which were destroyed because of their denial of truth. These deniers are those who are advancing further on the path of misguidance, and they have no thought of the Day of Judgment.

﴿وَإِن كُلٌّ لَّمَّا جَمِيعٌ لَّدَيْنَا مُحْضَرُونَ﴾ (36:32) "And all of them will certainly be brought before Us."

After this, cosmic proofs, miracles and signs are described. These are the signs which these people see day and night, and pass by with great carelessness. They exist within their own souls, they exist in their environment, and they exist in their ancient history, but they have no awareness of them, and when they are admonished they do not remember, they do not take a lesson.

﴿وَمَا تَأْتِيهِم مِّنْ آيَةٍ مِّنْ آيَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ إِلَّا كَانُوا عَنْهَا مُعْرِضِينَ﴾ (36:46) "Whenever a sign from the signs of their Lord comes to them, they turn away from it."

On the contrary, these people demand that the punishment of Allah come quickly, and they make this demand because they have no certainty that the punishment will come.

﴿وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا الْوَعْدُ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ (36:48) "They say: When will this promise be fulfilled, if you are truthful?"

Since these people demand the hastening of punishment and demand the coming of the Resurrection, while in their hearts they have no certainty that these matters will take place, a long scene from the scenes of the Resurrection is presented here. This scene clearly shows what the end will be, the arrival of which they are so eager for. This scene is described in such a manner as though their end has already occurred and they are seeing it.

Lesson No. 206: Explanation of the Verses

30 to 68

﴿يَا حَسْرَةً عَلَى الْعِبَادِ ۚ مَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾

Hasrah (regret) is a psychological state in which a person feels intense sorrow but has no power to change the situation. So he keeps looking and grieving, and he is pained. Allah does not feel regret over people's failure to believe. The meaning is that from the human point of view these people are worthy of regret. They deserve that their condition be lamented, because their state is most pitiable, distressing and deserving of compassion: on account of this misguidance they are about to be afflicted with perpetual evil and perpetual calamity.

Surely those are deserving of lament who are given the opportunity for salvation and do not benefit from it. Human history lies before them, yet they do not take warning from it, nor do they reflect on historical events. To these people Allah sends messengers from time to time for their guidance, but these people turn far from the doors of Allah's mercy and then even show disrespect toward the majesty of Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 36, verses 31–32:

اَلَمْ يَرَوْا كَمْ... لَا يَرْجِعُونَ (36:31) "Did they not see how many generations We destroyed before them, and that they never return to them?"

The peoples who were destroyed and wiped off the face of this world: in their being wiped out there is a lesson and a reminder for people. And the long history of humankind is a subject for reflection and contemplation for human beings. But these wretched people do not reflect upon human history, although, because of this heedlessness, they are advancing toward destruction and ruin. So what else can be done about their pitiful condition except to feel regret?

Even an animal, when it sees the death and destruction of another animal before its eyes, trembles and makes every effort within its capacity to escape that fate. But the state of human beings is that, despite seeing their own fellow beings destroyed because of their misguided conduct, they still walk the same path. Merely because of their pride, arrogance and heedlessness, they are deceived, and despite seeing, they walk the same path. A long history of humankind lies before them, and they even know that people were destroyed because of such and such causes, yet they still proceed like the blind, heedlessly, along the same paths, and do not see.

When those who were destroyed and given over to annihilation can no longer return to their successors, then these successors too will go along the same path. They will not be able to escape from Us. They too will be called to account.

وَإِن كُلٌّ لَّمَّا... مُحْضَرُونَ (36:32) "And indeed, all of them will certainly be brought before Us on a Day [of Judgement]."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 36, verses 33–35:

وایۃ لھم الارض المیتۃ۔۔۔۔۔ ومما لا یعلمون (33–36): Glorified is He who created all the pairs, whether from what the earth grows, or from themselves (i.e., humankind), or from things of which they have no knowledge.

These people deny the Messengers, yet they do not take lessons from the places of slaughter and the ruins of those who denied throughout human history. Nor do they learn a lesson from the state of creation, where people keep passing away and none of them returns. The Messenger's call is that he invites these people to Allah, the One whose existence is clearly indicated by this universe spread around them. It praises Allah and bears witness to His existence. This earth beneath their feet: they see that at one time it dies. There is no vegetation in it. Then it comes back to life. Living creatures come into being in it. Besides this, gardens are produced in it: date palms, grapes, and then springs gush forth within those gardens, and thus human and other life is seen flowing along.

Furthermore, this life is itself a miracle, and no human has the power to bring life into being, to create it, and then to set its chain of procreation in motion. The launching of this great miracle of life is a wondrous act of the Divine Power. The spirit of life is breathed into a dead body. On seeing the crop that grows moment by moment, the gardens with dense shade, and the ripe fruits full of them, the doors of the human heart and mind open. A person sees that these, tearing open the whole earth, push their heads out toward light and freedom. And this wood that pushes its head out becomes green and flourishing in the sunlight. Then this plant becomes adorned with leaves and fruits. Flowers bloom, fruits ripen and become fit for picking.

لیاکلوا ۔۔۔ ایدیھم (36:35): "So that they may eat of its fruit, and it was not their own hands that made it." It is the hand of Allah that enabled them to do this work, just as He gave the crops and fruits the capacity to grow.

افلا یشکرون (36:35): "Will they then not give thanks?"

After this, the Qur'an gives a subtle indication: the One who guided humankind to these plants and gardens is the One who also created pairs among the crops, namely male and female, just as there are pairs among humans and animals, and there are pairs among all other creation, of which only Allah has knowledge.

"Glory be to Him who created all the pairs, of what the earth produces, and of themselves, and of that which they do not know" (36:36). ”

This praise of Allah comes at a most fitting moment, and alongside the glorification it also manifests a great truth of this universe: that all of creation follows one pattern. Allah's creation has a principle, and it is this: Allah created all things in pairs. Plants too are in pairs, just like human beings, and apart from humans and plants, other creatures too are in pairs.

"And of that which they do not know" (36:36) — "and there are pairs among things they do not even know." This oneness of the principle of creation and design shows that the Creator of this universe is also one. This law operates fully within all forms, all groupings, all kinds, all species, all properties and all signs. It has now become known that the atom is the small part of this universe that has been discovered so far, and that the atom too is composed of two pairs, namely the positive and negative electronic rays. They are both separated from one another and united. Likewise, thousands of stars have become known that possess a dual (paired) creation: they are made of two stars, are arranged and harmonious with one another, and revolve in one and the same orbit, as though they are in the form of a well-ordered melody.

This is the dead land from which life springs forth. Now, moving beyond the earth, the Qur'an turns its attention to the heavens, and celestial scenes are presented before us, all of them wonders of divine power.

"And a sign for them is the night: We strip it of the day, and behold, they are plunged into darkness" (36:37) through "each floating in an orbit" (36:40).

The scene of the coming of night: the light ends and darkness gradually spreads. This is a scene that all human beings witness repeated every 24 hours, except in those regions where the cycle of night and day is repeated after six months, that is, in areas very close to the poles. Although this process is repeated again and again in the cycle of night and day, if one reflects upon it, it is a wonder of Allah's power and worthy of people's contemplation.

The manner of expression used for this wonder here is also unique. Here the night is imagined as being clothed in the day, and when the garment of the day is removed, the night comes, and people are suddenly plunged into darkness. This manner of expression can be understood in the following way, and it becomes reality rather than metaphor when we reflect upon the rotation of the earth on its axis. Because of this rotation, one point of the earth remains facing the sun and there it is day, while the part of the earth that goes out of view is suddenly stripped of the garment of day, and darkness again spreads over the environment. This scene continues in this manner with perfect order: at every moment the garment of day is pulled from the body of night, and night continues to appear. In short, this Qur'anic expression is both factual and also extremely eloquent and literary.

"And the sun runs on to its resting place" (36:38). The sun also has an axial rotation. It is generally thought that it is fixed in its place, but the latest scientific information is that the sun is not stationary but also moving, actually flowing. It is proceeding in one direction. In this vast universe, within this atmosphere and space, it is moving in one direction, and it moves in a single direction at a rate of 12 miles per second. But knowledge of its motion and speed belongs to Allah alone, who is All-Aware and All-Seeing. Allah clearly states that it has a fixed destination and that it moves toward it. How and when it reaches there is the Day of Resurrection, and knowledge of it belongs to Allah alone.

When we consider that the volume of this sun is a million times greater than the earth, and that this sun, along with its galaxy (and consider how vast the galaxy is!), is moving toward its resting place in a boundless expanse of space, then the knowledge and power of Allah can be gauged. This is the meaning of this verse.

"That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing" (36:38).

The moon—We have determined for it stations, until it returns like the old dried stalk of a date-palm. (36:39)

People can observe the moon through these stations. It appears like a crescent, then it keeps growing until it becomes full and round, like the full moon (badr). After that it begins to wane, and then it becomes like a crescent again, and appears just like an old, dry branch of the date-palm. Al-'Urjun (العرجون) refers to the branch on which the bunch of dates (the kind called "balah") grows. Those who watch the moon every night can enjoy this manner of expression of the Qur'an.

"Like the old dried stalk of a date-palm" (36:39). The word "qadim" (old) in this expression is especially meaningful. In the early nights the moon is a crescent, and in the last nights it is also a crescent, but in the early nights it appears fresh and full of growth, while in the last nights it presents a withered, declining scene, shrinking and drying up. It shrinks and becomes as dry as a dry branch. It is not mere coincidence that the Qur'an has adopted this manner of expression; rather it is purposeful and a true depiction of the real form, and it is remarkable.

By continuous reflection on moonlit nights, wondrous and fresh states of consciousness and imagination arise upon the curtains of human feeling, and profound effects are produced upon a person. The one who observes this moon and reflects upon it for a full month cannot help but be impressed, and cannot help but ask about the power of the Originator of the heavens, the Lord of majesty and beauty, who bestowed such beauty and such order upon these enormous celestial bodies. Every person can take guidance from this scene according to his capacity, whether or not he knows the secrets of this great universe. I say: the mere observation of the moon at night is sufficient to stir the human heart. It awakens consciousness and instills in a person the habit of reflection.

Now God draws attention to this vast universe and the subtle order of its celestial bodies, and to the phenomena that arise from this order and arrangement. Consider!

﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day; each is floating in an orbit.﴾ (36:40) Every star and planet has its own orbit (falak), or its own path. In its motion and rotation it cannot exceed its limits. Between the stars and planets there are immense distances. The distance between the earth and the sun is 73 million miles, and the moon is 240 million miles from the earth. Yet even these distances, despite their remoteness, are small within the cosmic scale: the nearest star to the sun, of the solar galaxy and of the nearest other galaxy, is four light-years away. In light-years, time is determined in such a way that it is the period in which light travels at a speed of 186,000 miles per second. Thus the star nearest to the galaxy of the sun is 104 million miles away.

God, who is the Creator of this universe, has created such immense distances between the stars and planets, and He who has prepared this wondrous plan of the great universe has done so in order that it be protected from mutual collision and clashing, and that this system continue as it is, unless God brings about the Resurrection. Therefore the sun does not have the power to overtake the moon, nor can the night come before the day or stand against it, because the rotation that produces night and day is ongoing. Hence neither of the two can get ahead of the other, nor can either block the path of the other.

﴿And each is floating in an orbit.﴾ (36:40) The movement of these planets and celestial bodies in the expanse of the cosmos is like a ship sailing in the sea. These ships, despite their greatness, are but a dark dot in that great ocean.

A person is astonished and bewildered when he sees that millions of planets and celestial bodies are scattered throughout this vast expanse of the cosmos and are floating. Around each planet and celestial body there is a vast space, and each is very far from the others; and despite the great size of these planets and bodies, within that vast space they are but a point. A very insignificant point!!

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 36, verses 41–42:

وایۃ لھم انا۔۔۔۔۔ الی حین (41 – 44). Here, within the context of the discourse, there is an extremely subtle connection. The stars and planets are floating in the vast expanse of the cosmos, and the ship filled with the descendants of Adam is sailing upon the waters. Between these two scenes there is an apparent relation, a correspondence of motion, and a link in that both have been subjected (made subservient) by Allah, and Allah has upheld them by His power within the heavens and the earth.

Both of these scenes are before the eyes of human beings, yet people do not reflect upon them. If a person opens his heart and broadens his mind, and reflects upon these and other matters, he can easily find the signs of Allah.

By the filled ship is perhaps meant the ship of Nuh (Noah), which carried the descendants of Adam. After that, Allah created for them other similar ships which carry people, and both of these were set in motion by the laws of nature that Allah placed in this universe, so that a ship floats on the surface of the waters. The planets float in the atmospheres of the heavens, and by means of wood, water and air, vapour or atomic power, they produce the force by which these huge ships move. All these matters are in accordance with the divine decree (taqdir ilahi).

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 36, verses 43–44:

﴿And if We wish, We drown them, and there is no one to cry for help to, nor are they rescued,﴾ [36:43] "If We wish, We drown them, none to hear their cry, and none can save them. It is only Our mercy that carries them across and grants them the opportunity to enjoy life for an appointed time." (36:44)

In the deep seas, the reality of a ship is the same as that of a feather in a storm. However heavy and large the ship may be, and however perfectly it may be built according to the most advanced scientific principles, if the mercy and compassion of Allah are not with those ships, they will be destroyed at any moment, by night or by day. Those who have travelled the seas, whether in a small boat or a large ocean liner, know well the terror of the sea. They know how minor human precautions are in comparison with the powerful waves of the sea. Therefore such people understand well the mercy of Allah.

The truth is that in this vast universe, against the storms and upheavals of the natural world, there is only the mercy of Allah, which has restrained the rebellious natural forces. In the heavens and the earth, there is no one other than Allah's power, the Hand of Divine Might, which holds all things together, until the Hour of Resurrection arrives at the time that Allah, the All-Wise, the All-Aware, has appointed for it.

﴿And an enjoyment for a time.﴾ [36:44] "Then it grants the opportunity to enjoy life until an appointed time."

Yet despite these most manifest signs, people sleep in the slumber of heedlessness. Their eyes do not fall upon these signs, their hearts do not awaken, and they do not give up their mockery and derisive manner. They have simply kept up the same refrain: "Just bring about the punishment with which you threaten us."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 36, verses 46–47:

"وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ..." to "...عَنْهَا مُعْرِضِينَ" (36:45–46): When it is said to them, "Beware of the punishment that lies before you and that has passed behind you, so that perhaps you may be shown mercy," they pay no heed. Whenever any of the signs of their Lord comes to them, they turn away from it without regard.

And when it is said to these people, "Spend from your wealth on the poor," they respond mockingly, saying:

﴿أَنُطْعِمُ مَن لَّوْ يَشَاءُ اللَّهُ أَطْعَمَهُ ۖ إِنْ أَنتُمْ إِلَّا فِي ضَلَالٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾ (36:47) "Shall we feed those whom, if God had willed, He would have fed Himself? You are only in manifest error." Beyond mockery, these people accuse those who call them to spend in charity of being in error.

The manner of their speech makes it clear that these people are utterly unaware of the divine laws (sunan Ilahiyyah) that operate throughout human life. The reality is that it is Allah who feeds everyone; Allah alone is the Provider of all. The wealth and sustenance that exist among people on earth are all created by Allah. Humans have created nothing for themselves, nor do they have power to create even a single thing. But it is Allah's will that human beings populate this earth. Therefore Allah made people dependent on their needs, and these needs can be met only through their own striving and effort: the arrangement of agriculture within the earth, the arrangement of industries, then the arrangement for transporting the earth's treasures from one place to another, then the supply and buying and selling of these goods in different times and by different methods. All these arrangements were made by Allah. Then people differ and vary in their abilities and capacities, and Allah, according to His will, grants different capacities to different people, so that humans together may carry out the duties of vicegerency (khilafah) on earth. The variation in human capacities is not only in gathering wealth and property. Sometimes people are occupied with other needs, and these other fields are also demanded by the requirements of vicegerency. Therefore some people are not free for the work of gathering wealth and are materially in need. On one side there are the broad requirements of the human office of vicegerency on earth, and on the other side there are the capacities to fulfil those requirements. In accordance with these capacities, needs and benefits are exchanged among people, and competition and the determination of shares take place among them. This is a vast economic system with countless links, each linked to the next, and it even extends across generations: that is, from generation to generation there are causes that affect people's economic striving. In short, in the field of economics, Allah placed differences in wealth and sustenance among people on the basis of diverse and varied causes. In its reality, this difference was placed so that humans, while fulfilling the requirements of the office of vicegerency, would strive for the building and progress of this earth. However, to keep this difference within the bounds of moderation, Islam has also provided a remedy for certain individual deprivations: it is obligatory upon the wealthy to set aside a portion of their wealth for the poor and the deprived, and no single individual in society should remain deprived of basic economic necessities. Through these arrangements, the moral and psychological reform of the rich and the poor is achieved. For this spending, Islam takes zakat, and the linguistic meaning of zakat includes the sense of purification. Thus this spending is both a purification of wealth and an act of worship. And through it, Allah has also established a bond of love and friendship between the poor and the rich.

Therefore, the statement of those who lack the capacity to grasp the wisdom of divine providence:

﴿أَنُطْعِمُ مَن لَّوْ يَشَاءُ اللَّهُ أَطْعَمَهُ﴾ (36:47) "Shall we feed those whom, if God had willed, He would have fed Himself?" And upon this, further, the accusation against those who call them to spend:

﴿إِنْ أَنتُمْ إِلَّا فِي ضَلَالٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾ (36:47) "You are only in manifest error." In truth, this is real error, and these people are unaware of the divine laws operating in this universe. These people are also unaware of the genuine course of life in this world and its diverse economic causes. Furthermore, they are unaware of the purposes for which Allah has given people diverse capacities in this world, and as a result of which people do different work, and because of which the exchange of the means of livelihood takes place and the economic system of the world keeps running.

Islam establishes an economic system in which all people have freedom to work and opportunities to pursue their various kinds of work. The Islamic system then also provides all people with free opportunities for various types of work. People thus live pure and clean lives, and afterwards, through their practical measures, they take special steps to resolve economic imbalances. Finally, the discussion turns to their doubt concerning resurrection after death, and because of which they used to mock those who held that belief.

They say: "When will this threat (of the Resurrection) be fulfilled? Tell them: if you are truthful." (36:48) Allah has fixed the time for the occurrence of the Resurrection, and it cannot come before its time because of human haste or insistence. And even if people hope that it will occur somewhat beyond its appointed time, this too is not possible, for with Allah everything is according to a measure. Every event occurs at its appointed time. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 36, verses 49–53:

ما ینظرون الا۔۔۔۔۔۔ جمیع لدینا محضرون (49 – 53) "۔ "۔ جھٹلانے والوں کا سوال یہ تھا۔

ویقولون متی ھذا۔۔۔۔۔ صدقین (36: 48) "یہ قیامت کی دھمکی کب پوری ہوگی؟ بتاؤ اگر تم سچے ہو"۔ لہٰذا ان کا جواب اس منظر کی شکل میں دیا گیا۔

ما ینظرون الا۔۔۔۔ الی اھلھم یرجعون (36: 49 – 50) "دراصل یہ جس چیز کی راہ تک رہے ہیں وہ بس ایک دھماکہ ہے جو یکایک انہیں عین اس حالت میں دھرلے گا جب یہ جھگڑ رہے ہوں گے اور اس وقت یہ وصیت تک نہ کرسکیں گے اور نہ اپنے گھروں کو پلٹ سکیں گے"۔ قیامت اچانک لوگوں کو اپنی گرفت میں لے لے گی، اس وقت وہ اپنے دنیاوی جھگڑوں یا مذہبی مباحثوں میں مصروف ہوں گے اور ان کو وقوع قیامت کی امید ہی نہ ہوگی۔ اور نہ وہ اسے کچھ اہمیت دیں گے۔ لیکن وہ اچانک واقع ہوجائے گی۔ ہر شخص اسی حال میں گرفتار ہوگا۔ جس پر وہ اس وقت ہوگا۔ کسی کو آنے والوں کے بارے میں نہ وصیت کے مواقع ہوں گے۔ اور نہ ان کو اس قدر مہلت ہوگی کہ وہ گھر تک چلا جائے اور گھر والوں کے بارے میں نہ وصیت کے مواقع ہوں گے۔ اور نہ ان کو اس قدر مہلت ہوگی کہ وہ گھر تک چلا جائے اور گھر والوں سے کچھ کہہ دے۔ اور وہ ہوں گے کہاں؟ کیونکہ گھر والے بھی جہاں ہوں گے اسی قیامت کی گرفت میں ہوں گے۔

اور اس کے بعد صور پھونکا جائے گا۔ ہر شخص اپنی قبر سے اٹھے گا اور جلدی سے دوڑ پڑے گا۔ یہ انتہائی درجے میں ہیبت زدہ اور دہشت زدہ ہوگا۔ ہر شخص دوسرے سے پوچھے گا۔

من بعثنا من مرقدنا (36: 52) "ارے یہ کس نے ہماری خوابگاہ سے ہمیں اٹھا کر کھڑا کیا؟" قدرے وقفے کے بعد اب دہشت ختم ہوگی تو اصل حقیقت ان کو معلوم ہوجائے گی۔

ھذا ما وعد۔۔۔۔ المرسلون (36: 52) "یہ وہی چیز ہے جس کا خدائے رحمن نے وعدہ کیا تھا اور رسولوں کی بات سچی تھی" اور اب آخری آواز ہوگی۔ ایک پکار اور یہ تمام بکھرے ہوئے پریشان اور حیران لوگ اللہ کے حضور حاضر ہوں گے۔

فاذاھم جمیع لدینا محضرون (36: 53) "اچانک سب کے سب ہمارے سامنے حاضر کر دئیے جائیں گے"۔ اور سب کے سب صفوں کی صورت میں منظم کر دئیے جائیں گے اور یہ پیشی چشم زدن میں ہوگی اور صدائے بازگشت کی طرح ہوگی اور اس وقفہ و محل پر اللہ کا یہ فیصلہ سنایا جائے گا اور اعلان ہوگا کہ جزاء و سزائیں کسی کے ساتھ کوئی بےانصافی نہ ہوگی۔

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 36, verse 54:

﴿So today no soul will be wronged in the least, and you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do.﴾ "Here, with great swiftness, three scenes are glimpsed, and the doubts and misgivings of those who needlessly doubt the occurrence of the Resurrection are refuted, and all in a most orderly arrangement. Now, the account of the believers is also wrapped up in a few moments, and their end is also shown swiftly."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 36, verses 55–58:

ان اصحب الجنۃ۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ من رب رحیم (55 – 58) ” “۔

They will be occupied in pleasures and delights. Divine favours will rain down upon them, and they will sit in the most pleasant shade. Reclining on couches face to face, they will be the masters of Paradise, and it will be their right that whatever they desire will be provided for them. Over and above these delights, their spouses will also be with them. And they will be honoured to such an extent that Allah Himself will send greetings of peace upon them. This will be their distinction from the Lord, the Most Generous.

﴿Peace, a word from a Lord Most Merciful﴾ (36:58). It is as though the words "from a Lord Most Merciful" present the greeting of peace to them. As for the disbelievers, the reckoning and accounting of their case is not shown here; rather, here they are merely rebuked, reproached and blamed.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 36, verses 59–64:

Wamtazu al-yawma ayyuha... bima kuntum takfurun (59–64): Their hospitality will be contempt and humiliation.

"Wamtazu al-yawma ayyuha al-mujrimun" (36:59): "And separate yourselves today, O criminals." Separate yourselves from the people of faith and stand apart from them.

"Alam a'had ilaykum..." to "...aduwwun mubin" (36:60): "Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan? Indeed, he is a clear enemy to you." Addressing them with "O children of Adam" shames them, because it was Satan who expelled their father from Paradise. Despite this, you worship him, though he is your clear enemy.

"Wa-ani'budoni..." to "...mustaqim" (36:61): "And that you should worship Me. This is the straight path." This path leads to Me, and by following it My pleasure is attained. You did not fear that enemy who led your generations and groups astray.

"Afalam takunu ta'qilun" (36:62): "Did you not have reason?" At this point the punishment prescribed for them is announced here, which is extremely painful. And this judgment is also pronounced in a manner of severity and rebuke.

"Hadhihi jahannamu..." to "...takfurun" (36:63–64): "This is the Hell with which you were being warned, so burn in it today for the disbelief you used to commit in the world." This hearing does not end here and its proceedings are not wound up; rather, the discussion on this subject continues and a new scene comes before us.

On Surah 36, verse 65:

Today We shall seal their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn. [Qur'an 36:65] Thus they blame one another. Their own limbs bear witness against them, and their very personality breaks into pieces; the parts of their being become witnesses against one another, and every limb of a human being will be individually accountable before its Lord. Before Allah, every limb will confess its sin and submit in surrender. This is an extremely terrifying and frightening scene. A person trembles at the very thought of this scene.

This scene concludes with their tongues being sealed, while their hands are conversing and their feet are bearing witness, although they never expected such a thing from their hands and feet. Had Allah willed, He would have dealt with them in some other manner, and He would have given them whatever punishment He wished, and brought upon them whatever calamity He willed. Here Allah also gives two examples of other punishments. Had He willed, it would have happened thus.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 36, verses 66–67:

"And if We willed, We would have obliterated their eyes... and they would not return." (36:66–67)

These are two scenes. In them there is both punishment and chastisement, and also contempt and mockery. The contempt is directed at those who deny the call of Islam, and the mockery is directed at those who ridicule the religion of Islam. They used to say:

﴿Matä hädhā al-waʿdu in kuntum ṣādiqīn﴾ (36:48): "When will this promise be fulfilled, if you are truthful?"

Accordingly, in the first scene, their forms are distorted and they are made blind. Among the blind there is a contest of who can advance ahead of the others. They cross the path and push ahead of one another, yet they do not find the way as the blind do not. They advance stumbling and falling. So how is it possible for them to see the straight path?

﴿Fa-annā yubṣirūn﴾ (36:66): "How then could they be guided to the path?"

In the second scene they are shown as having stopped in their places while walking, having become statues that can neither advance nor retreat, even though these people were still blind and were groping about in every direction.

In these two scenes they appear as toys, such toys that on seeing them one involuntarily laughs. These were the same people who used to mock the occurrence of the Resurrection and did not give it any importance.

This will be their condition at the time the Resurrection takes place, which they are so eager for. But even if they are granted respite on the earth, and they progress greatly in it and develop it, and they remain alive on it until the Day of Resurrection according to Allah's plan, they will still reach a state of such abhorrence that instead of living in it, they will prefer to die quickly. These people will become so weak and aged, and their physical and mental powers will become so enfeebled, that they will not understand anything.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 36, verse 68:

﴿And whomever We cause to live long, We reverse him in creation. Will they not then understand?﴾ (68)

When a person becomes very old, he reverts once more, becoming a weak child. But in him there is none of the endearing charm and attraction of a child. Thus the aged keep moving backward. The knowledge they once had, they keep forgetting. Their nerves keep growing weaker. Their thinking keeps declining. Their capacity to endure keeps diminishing. A time comes when such a person becomes a pure child. The difference is that when a child speaks with a lisp, it sounds pleasing; people look at him and smile. And if he commits some foolishness, the onlookers are still delighted. But the old man is downcast. His foolishness can be borne only with compassion and respect. And as his powers decline and foolish acts proceed from him, people make jokes at his expense. As he becomes frail and his back bends, he keeps retreating. In both conditions this is a bad end, which awaits those who deny the Islamic call. These are the people whom Allah has deprived of guidance and right direction because of their deeds, and the honour that was to be theirs through faith has passed them by, leaving them deprived of it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 36, verse 69:

Lesson No. 207: Explanation of the Verses

69 ... to ... 83

This is the final lesson of this surah, and it takes up all the issues that form the axis of the surah: the question of revelation, the nature of revelation, the question of divinity and the oneness of God, resurrection after death, and gathering and dispersal (on the Day of Judgment). In this lesson all these issues are presented separately, one after another, in a highly impactful and forceful manner. Across all the topics it is shown that the power of divine will is at work in the creation of everything, and that the keys to this universe are in the hand of Allah. This theme is stated in this lesson and in the last verse of the surah.

﴿Glory be to Him in whose hand is the complete sovereignty over everything, and to Him you will be returned﴾ (36:83). These are the works of divine power and its craftsmanship: He created the cattle for mankind and made them subservient to them. He who created man from a lowly drop of semen, and created him from a very small drop, will likewise recreate him from decayed bones. He who produced fire from the green tree. He who created a great universe like the heavens and the earth, and who is the owner and supreme authority over everything in this world. This is the summary of this surah.

﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him...﴾ (36:69–70)

The subject of revelation was discussed at the very beginning of the surah.

﴿Ya, Sin. By the Wise Qur'an, indeed you are among the messengers, upon a straight path. It is the revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful, that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are heedless﴾ (36:1–6). Here the mention of revelation comes in the context that it is divine revelation and not poetry. Some people used to accuse the Prophet ﷺ of being a poet and the Qur'an of being a particular kind of poetic speech. In fact, the leaders of Quraysh knew that the matter was not so. The words brought by Muhammad ﷺ are, according to the styles of Arabic poetry, neither poetry nor prose in the style of their prose. This accusation was in reality a propaganda war waged by them against Islam, and the charge against the Qur'an and the Messenger ﷺ was made to mislead the common people. Yes, these people would argue from the beauty and elegance and the unique and impactful eloquence of the Qur'an. In this way the common people could not distinguish between poetry and the Qur'an, and therefore they were influenced by this propaganda.

Here Allah refutes the claim that We taught the Prophet ﷺ poetry: when Allah did not teach him the knowledge of poetry, he could not have had knowledge of poetry, because a person knows only what Allah teaches him.

After this, Allah also unveils the fact that composing poetry is not befitting to him (wa ma yanbaghi lahu), because the method of poetry is very different from the method of prophethood. Poetry is an impression and an expression of impressions, and human impressions change in different circumstances, whereas the method of prophethood is based on revelation and is constant. The prophet follows a straight path and adheres to the divine law according to which this entire universe moves, and this law does not change according to changing desires and changing impressions, just as poetry changes, and in every state there is no single doctrine found in poetry.

In prophethood, the prophet is always directly connected with Allah, receives guidance directly from Allah's revelation, and his struggle is of a lasting nature, so that the system of life runs according to the commands of Allah. Whereas poetry, even at its high standard, consists merely of human desires and impressions of beauty and perfection. Human thought contains shortcomings and weaknesses, and poetry reflects the limited conceptions of man and is the product of man's limited capacity and knowledge. When this poetry falls from its station, it is reduced merely to physical pleasure, natural desires, and sexual gratification. After that it becomes a name for bodily fever. Therefore prophethood and poetry are different in their nature and essence. Even if poetry is of the highest grade, it consists of desires that rise from the earth, whereas prophethood descends from the heavens in the form of guidance.

﴿It is nothing but a reminder and a clear Qur'an﴾ (36:69). "Dhikr" and "Qur'an" are both attributes of one and the same thing. "Dhikr" in the sense that the real purpose of this book is admonition, and "Qur'an" in the sense that it is recited. It is, as it were, the remembrance of Allah in which the heart is occupied, and it is the Qur'an that is recited by the tongue, and it has been revealed so that it may fulfil its noble purpose.

﴿لِيُنذِرَ مَن كَانَ حَيًّا وَيَحِقَّ الْقَوْلُ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ (36:70) "تاکہ وہ ہر اس شخص کو خبردار کر دے جو زندہ ہو اور انکار کرنے والوں پر حجت تمام ہوجائے"۔ قرآن نے کفر اور حیات کو بالمقابل رکھا ہے۔ گویا کفر موت کے ہم معنی ہے۔ اور جس شخص کے دل میں ایمان کی استعداد ہو، وہ زندہ ہے اور قرآن کا مقصد یہ ہے کہ وہ رسول اللہ (ﷺ) پر اس لیے نازل ہوا ہے تاکہ آپ اس کے ذریعے ان لوگوں کو ڈرائیں جو زندہ ہوں، جن لوگوں کے اندر زندگی کی رمق ہو، وہ مر نہ گئے ہوں تاکہ ڈرانے کا انہیں فائدہ ہو۔ رہے کفار تو وہ مردے ہوتے ہیں۔ ان کو ڈرانے کا کوئی فائدہ نہیں ہوتا۔ نیز ڈرانے کا فریضہ اس لیے عائد کیا گیا ہے تاکہ وہ عذاب کے مستحق ہوجائیں کیونکہ اللہ تعالیٰ اس وقت تک کسی کو سزا نہیں دیتا جب تک اس تک اللہ کا پیغام پہنچ نہ جائے اور پھر وہ کفر نہ کر دے۔ اور پھر اگر اللہ انہیں ہلاک کر دے تو وہ بلا حجت اور بغیر سبب کے ہلاک نہ کیا جائے۔

یوں لوگوں کو معلوم ہوجاتا ہے کہ قرآن کے حوالے سے لوگ دو قسم کے ہوتے ہیں۔ ایک فریق وہ ہے جو اسے قبول کرتا ہے تو وہ زندہ ہے اور ایک وہ ہے جو قبول نہیں کرتا تو وہ مردہ ہے۔ اور اس فریق کو معلوم ہوجائے کہ اس کے خلاف فیصلہ برحق ہوا اور وہ سزا کا مستحق ہوجاتا ہے۔

اس سبق کے دوسرے ٹکڑے میں الوہیت اور وحدانیت کا مضمون بیان ہوا ہے۔ الوہیت اور وحدانیت کا یہ بیان لوگوں کے مشاہدات کے فریم ورک میں ہے کہ ذرا دیکھو کہ اللہ کے ان پر کس قدر انعامات ہیں جنہیں وہ استعمال کر رہے ہیں لیکن اللہ کا شکر ادا نہیں کرتے۔

Do they not see that We have created for them, of what Our hands have made, cattle which they own? (Qur'an 36:71 is the opening of this passage; the commentary begins below.)

Do they not see? The signs of Allah lie right before them, visible to all. They are neither hidden from them nor far away. Nor are these signs so intricate that grasping them requires deep reflection. These bounties which Allah created for human beings and made them the owners of are, among them, the animals that have been made subservient to humans, on which they ride, and of which some they eat and drink. From some they derive other benefits, and all these matters are in accordance with Allah's arrangements (tadbir) and decrees (taqdir). Then Allah bestowed on human beings various capabilities and distinctive qualities, and then endowed the animals with various characteristics and capabilities. He gave humans the power to make them obedient to them and to benefit from them. Thus they were tamed, made obedient, and through them various needs and necessities of humans have continued to be fulfilled. Human beings did not have the power to create these blessings by themselves. Leaving aside all the blessings, even if all of humanity gathered together and wished to create a single fly, they would not be able to do so. Moreover, since Allah did not place in the fly the quality of becoming subservient to humans, humans have to this day been unable to make the fly subservient.

Then will they not be grateful? (36:73) "Will they not then be grateful?" When a person thinks about these matters in this manner and reflects upon them in the light of the Holy Qur'an, he reaches the conclusion that he is immersed in Allah's blessings, and that the rain of His generosity is pouring down upon him at every moment. Everything in his environment is a mercy for him. Whenever he rides an animal, or eats a piece of meat, or drinks a sip of milk, or wears a garment of cotton, wool or silk, or uses ghee and butter, or puts his blessings to use, he gains a profound awareness of how vast the mercy of the Creator of the universe is, and how great the scope of His blessings is. This awareness becomes even firmer when a person consumes the fresh and the stored crops and fruits of this world, and as a result of this awareness, the whole of human life becomes praise and glorification. At every step, because of this awareness, a person worships and serves, and day and night is a praiser of Allah.

﴿And they have taken gods besides Allah, hoping that they might be helped. They are not able to help them, but they are a host brought forward for them.﴾ (36:74–75)

In the past, idols and shrines were worshipped, or trees and stars were worshipped. Angels and jinn were worshipped. The idolatry of the past is still found in some regions today. But those who are not caught up in this manifest worship are also not believers in pure tawhid (pure monotheism). Today most people fear false and worthless powers other than Allah and rely on supports other than Allah. Shirk certainly has many forms, and its shapes and styles keep changing with differences of time and place.

These people served those deities so that through them they would attain success. In practice, however, the situation was that if anyone took action against their deities, these people would stand up to support their deities and defend them. In reality, these people were helpers of their worthless gods.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 36, verse 75:

﴿And they are an army brought forward for them.﴾ [36:75] "They were ready soldiers for their gods." This was the extreme weakness of their thinking and reasoning. Even today, the majority of people are afflicted with this same way of thinking, and the difference is only in outward form. The underlying thought has no difference. Those who have made great tyrants and dictators their gods today are not far from the idol-worshippers of earlier ages. In reality, these people are the army guards of those idols. They support them, worship them, and also defend and protect them.

Idol-worship is, after all, idol-worship. Its form may differ, but it exists in every age. And whenever the belief in Tawhid (Divine Oneness) becomes unsettled, idol-worship appears in some form, and shirk (associating partners with God) and jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) take its place. The salvation and deliverance of humanity lies only in pure Tawhid, in which Allah alone is regarded as the deity. Only His servitude is performed, only Him is relied upon, and obedience and veneration are also directed to Him alone.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 36, verse 76:

﴿So let not their speech grieve you. Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they reveal.﴾ (36:76)

The address here is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The people he was addressing were those who had taken others besides Allah as deities, and these people used to be ungrateful to Allah. Consequently, they also did not accept advice. The Messenger (ﷺ) was told not to concern himself with them, for Allah knows them well. The schemes they are devising against the Islamic movement and in favour of idol-worship are within Our sight. Therefore, O Messenger, you are not responsible for these matters. Their affairs lie open before Divine power, and Allah's power encompasses them.

When the workers of the Islamic movement hold this belief, their situation becomes very easy. Since they rely solely on Allah, there remains no danger for them, because they are certain that Allah knows both the outward and the inward. That they are in Allah's control and within Allah's sight, even though this may not be apparent to the eye.

This is the third part of this final lesson. In it, the matter of resurrection and gathering is taken up.

﴿Does not man see that We created him from a drop of semen, and behold, he becomes an open adversary?﴾ (36:77) through ﴿Be! And it is.﴾ (36:82)

In this part, the discussion begins by directing man to look at his own existence and his own self. How his creation began, how he grew, and how he reached the age of maturity: all these stages that were traversed in his life are before his eyes. He has been watching them. Does he not take from them some lesson and admonition? Can he not derive from the creation and formation of human life itself the lesson that raising him up again for Allah is not a difficult task, even if he has perished and his bones have decayed?

﴿Does not man see that We created him from a drop of semen, and behold, he becomes an open adversary?﴾ (36:77). "Does man not see that We created him from a drop, and then he stood up as a clear disputer."

The question is: what is that drop of semen, about which man thinks that it is the close origin of man? It is composed of a worthless fluid; it is not a solid thing and it has no value. It is a fluid in which there are thousands of cells. Out of these thousands of cells, only one embryo is formed, and this one embryo then becomes a human being. Then this human being speaks insolently to his Lord and Creator, opposes his Lord, and demands proof and argument from his Creator.

Whereas it is the Creator, the Capable, who made man from such a contemptible thing, and he became an "open adversary" and a clear disputer. Let there be consideration of what he has become. Let there be a look at his beginning and his end. Is it a difficult matter before that Capable Power to reassemble the parts of the body, even though, after dying, they have scattered in the earth?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 36, verses 78–79:

"And he presents to Us a comparison and forgets his own creation. He says: 'Who will give life to these bones when they have decayed?' Say: 'He will give them life who brought them into being the first time, and He is Knowing of every creation.'" How simple is this logic! It is a most natural argument, one that appears in accordance with observation. This drop of semen, what is it, that it is worth more than decayed bones? Was not man made from this very semen? And is not the process of creating a human being a second creation, as the first creation was? And He who made man from that base drop and gave him the personality by which he became a clear disputer, can He not form a human from these decayed bones, and from these same elements produce a new creation? This matter is very easy and evident, and it is so evident that no question even arises about it, let alone that anyone should debate it.

"Say: He will give them life who brought them into being the first time, and He is Knowing of every creation" (36:79).

Afterwards, Allah shows them an example of His creative power and the nature of His creation so that this matter settles in their minds. This craftsmanship of Allah is among what they observe and among their daily routines, and they keep testing it.
